name: MN-05
label: Safe D

key_factors: District partisan lean of D+32 makes this among the most Democratic House seats
Omar's fundraising dominance: $6.4M raised and $1.3M on hand versus $89K for Nagel
Prediction markets price the race around 96% Democratic
No public general-election polls or expert ratings to refine the estimate
model.rationale: A D+32 district, a well-funded incumbent with no reported outside opposition, and markets pricing the race near 96% Democratic leave little room for an upset. The genuine uncertainty concerns the size of the margin, not the winner.
model.watch: A late wave of Republican outside spending or unexpected polling showing a far narrower race would be the main reason to revisit this forecast.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Minneapolis-based MN-05 is one of the most Democratic-leaning House districts in the country, and incumbent Ilhan Omar is seeking another term with the advantages that come with it. She has raised more than $6.3 million and holds over $1.2 million on hand, while Republican John Nagel has roughly $89,000 available. No outside spending against her has been reported, and prediction markets put her chances around 96%.

With no public general-election polling and no expert ratings to consult, the outlook rests on district fundamentals. A partisan lean of D+32, a favorable national environment, incumbency, and the money gap all point to a comfortable Democratic win. The main unknown is the size of the margin rather than the outcome, though low-turnout dynamics can shift results by a few points in either direction.
